title: Hefazat-led march from Baitul Mukarram toward the French Embassy demanding Bangladesh cut diplomatic ties
location: Dhaka: Baitul Mukarram National Mosque through central Dhaka to Shantinagar/French Embassy approach
scope: One-day march and rally led by Hifazat and allied Islamist groups
organizer: Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh with Somomona Islami Dal / allied Islamist organizations
participants_original: UNB/Daily Star: several hundred; New Age and bdnews24: thousands. Estimates differ but each is above threshold.
threshold_50_evidence: All body accounts clearly describe several hundred or thousands in the same gathering; threshold is supported qualitatively despite incompatible estimates.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: UNB says several hundred and New Age/bdnews24 report thousands at Baitul Mukarram-to-Shantinagar event.

demands.summary: bdnews24 and New Age report explicit calls to Bangladesh government and Parliament on diplomatic ties/condemnation.

start_date.summary: Contemporary event reports date the rally and march to 2 November, starting at Baitul Mukarram.

location.summary: Central Dhaka from Baitul Mukarram to Shantinagar where police blocked the march.

state_response.summary: Police blocked the route, forced/turned the march back and traffic resumed after participants dispersed; no killings, arrests or state violence established.

notes: The event called for French-product boycotts, but the coded state target is domestic: cut Bangladesh-France ties, pass a parliamentary condemnation motion, lodge an official protest, or close/expel French mission. Daily Star article is UNB-origin and not a second independent written source. bdnews24 and New Age are separate reporting. This is distinct from the 27 October Islami Andolan march: separate organizer, six-day gap, and reports describe 27 October as ended that day.
open_questions: Independent reviewer should compare estimates and confirm state-demand coding/episode boundary.

title: Oikya Parishad organized minority-protection protests and sit-ins in Dhaka and Chittagong
location: Dhaka Shahbagh/National Museum and Chittagong New Market; organizers announced simultaneous programs across Bangladesh
scope: Nationally coordinated rallies and sit-ins, with contemporaneous evidence from Dhaka and Chittagong
organizer: Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Oikya Parishad and member associations
participants_original: Dhaka: nearly 500 people from 10 associations (Dhaka Tribune copy of UNB); Chittagong: several hundred / nearly 1,000 / thousands across JagoNews24 same-day reports.
threshold_50_evidence: Dhaka report says nearly 500; Chittagong reports several hundred or around a thousand. Both locations clearly exceed 50. Do not add local estimates into a national total.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Nearly 500 reported in Dhaka; several hundred/around 1,000 reported at Chittagong New Market.

demands.summary: Dhaka and Chittagong reports attribute protection/investigation/commission demands directly to Bangladesh government and state policy.

start_date.summary: Reports place the organized gatherings on 7 November; Chittagong began around 9:45am and Dhaka procession around 11am.

location.summary: Dhaka Shahbagh and Chittagong New Market are documented; nationwide program was announced but other cities are not individually specified in opened bodies.

state_response.summary: Dhaka/Chittagong police were alert; sources do not document arrests, force or dispersal. Unknown.

notes: This is not coded as an intercommunal dispute: protesters addressed Bangladesh’s government over protection, investigations, a national minority commission and constitutional policy. Dhaka Tribune’s Dhaka-origin report explicitly credits UNB; JagoNews24 is a separate Chittagong account. Its two same-day articles are one outlet and likely one reporting family, not independent counts. Parallel, nationally announced program supports national organization; only Dhaka/Chittagong locations are concretely evidenced here.
open_questions: Check if other locations in the announced national program have independently attributable counts; no total can be inferred.
Independent reviewer should decide whether domestic state-directed demands and national event linkage are sufficiently supported.

title: Muktijuddho Mancha Shahbagh demonstration for government action on sculpture opponents
location: Raju Memorial sculpture to Shahbagh intersection, Dhaka
threshold_50_evidence: Source documents a procession and one-hour blockade but no crowd estimate; traffic interruption is not a headcount.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No published count or qualitative crowd estimate.

demands.summary: The body attributes a demand for tough government action/arrests and broader state policy changes.

start_date.summary: Source dates the procession/blockade to 28 November.

location.summary: Raju Memorial sculpture to Shahbagh, Shahbagh intersection, Dhaka.

state_response.summary: One-hour traffic blockade described; no police response, force or arrests in opened report.

notes: Participants demanded arrest/action against named Islamist leaders and a seven-point charter including a ban on religion-based politics. It is not an election-support rally on available evidence, but threshold remains unknown. The announced 1 December nationwide action is a future program and is not imported into this event.
open_questions: Find a contemporaneous attendance estimate and any state response.
